slot.brief: Ask which of the given aqueous ions (e.g. Sc3+, Ti3+, Cu+, Zn2+, V3+) is colourless and why, or which listed ion shows a stated colour.

stem: Which aqueous ion characteristically forms a blue solution due to transitions within a partially filled $d$ subshell?

verdicts.working: Aqueous Cu²⁺ is characteristically blue because of d–d transitions; Co²⁺ is typically pink, Ni²⁺ green, and Zn²⁺ colorless.

working:
$\text{Cu}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}]\,3d^9$ (partially filled $d$ subshell) $\longrightarrow$ blue aqueous solution.

Independent check: Aqueous Cu²⁺ is characteristically blue because of d–d transitions; Co²⁺ is typically pink, Ni²⁺ green, and Zn²⁺ colorless.
solution:
Aqueous $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ has a partially filled $3d^9$ subshell, allowing $d$–$d$ transitions that produce its characteristic blue colour.
Thus, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ forms a blue solution.
